title: The Diagram Lemmas in an Abelian Category

items.title: Short five lemma in an abelian category
items.strategy: Chase a member across the two short exact rows. The monic half uses the member-cancellation rule, the epic half uses exactness plus the member-surjectivity rule, and the isomorphism clause combines the two halves.

items.title: A morphism of short exact sequences with invertible outer maps is invertible
items.strategy: Apply the short five lemma to obtain that the middle vertical is both monic and epic, then invoke balancedness of abelian categories.

items.title: Short five lemma by pullback without members
items.strategy: Replace the member chase by pullback and exactness comparisons. Pulling back the right square transfers kernels, pulling back the left square transfers cokernels dually, and balancedness again turns the mono-plus-epi conclusion into an isomorphism.

items.title: Snake data
The connecting morphism exists and is unique
items.strategy: Follow Mac Lane's arrow-theoretic route. Form the pullback against ker(gamma) and the dual pushout against coker(alpha), show the middle composite vanishes against the kernel and cokernel on its two sides, and factor it uniquely through ker(gamma) and coker(alpha).

items.title: The connecting morphism depends on no choices
Snake lemma in an abelian category
items.strategy: Splice the connecting morphism into the already-known two-node kernel and cokernel rows. Exactness at the connecting term is the one place where the subtraction-surrogate rule is spent, while the endpoint exactness comes from the earlier kernel/cokernel comparison theorem.

items.title: Snake lemma under the weaker Stacks hypotheses
items.strategy: Use the Stacks shape with only one zero at each end. The same connecting-arrow construction still applies, and the published kernel/cokernel exactness lemma supplies the endpoint mono and epi clauses without silently strengthening the hypotheses.

items.title: The arrow category of an abelian category
Naturality of the connecting morphism
items.strategy: A morphism of snake data is itself snake data in the arrow category. Apply the connecting-morphism construction there and read the resulting arrow back componentwise; uniqueness forces the square of connecting morphisms to commute.

items.title: The kernel-cokernel sequence of a composite is a snake
items.strategy: Place the composite f followed by g into the standard short-exact-sequence diagram whose kernels and cokernels were already published, then identify the resulting snake sequence with the published composite sequence term by term.

items.title: Four lemma in an abelian category
items.strategy: Factor the relevant middle arrows through their images so that the four-column window becomes a snake-lemma diagram. Apply the snake lemma once for the epic half and dually for the monic half.

items.title: Weak four lemma with the exactness hypotheses named
items.strategy: Translate the named-node exactness assumptions into the exact four-column windows needed for the four lemma by adjoining the displayed zeros explicitly and using the degenerate exactness criteria.

items.title: The two halves of the four lemma are mutually dual
Sharp five lemma in an abelian category
items.strategy: Apply the two halves of the four lemma to the left and right four-column windows. The monic and epic conclusions use different windows and different outer assumptions, exactly as in the sharp source statements.

items.title: Five lemma in an abelian category
items.strategy: Specialize the sharp five lemma to the case where the two middle comparison maps are isomorphisms, so the center map is both monic and epic, and conclude by balancedness.

items.title: Why the five lemma asks for isomorphisms in the middle
Half nine lemma
items.strategy: Run the weak four lemma down the left edge of the 3 x 3 diagram so that exactness of two rows propagates to the third one node at a time. The lemma isolates the left-exact half that the full nine lemma later dualizes.

items.title: Nine lemma in an abelian category
items.strategy: Apply the half nine lemma once and then apply its dual to the opposite diagram. This packages the two one-sided implications into the standard top-row iff bottom-row statement when the middle row and all columns are short exact.

items.title: Nine lemma variants by which rows are assumed exact
items.strategy: Read off the top-row and bottom-row cases from the nine lemma, then isolate the middle-row case and record the extra zero-composite hypothesis that makes the remaining row into a complex before exactness is addressed.

items.title: Why the middle nine lemma needs a zero composite
Sharp nine lemma
items.strategy: Reuse the half nine lemma in the left-exact setup, then add the extra short-exact hypotheses only where they are actually spent to upgrade left exactness of the first row to short exactness.

items.title: Symmetric nine lemma
items.strategy: Combine the sharp nine lemma with its dual and then rotate through the remaining rows and columns. Once three of the four surrounding exactness conditions are known, the fourth is forced by the same argument in one orientation or the other.

items.title: The nine lemma follows from the snake lemma
items.strategy: Apply the snake lemma to the two adjacent rows of the 3 x 3 diagram after replacing one corner object by the relevant image. The resulting exact sequence forces the missing row exactness.

items.title: The splitting lemma follows from the nine lemma
items.strategy: Insert a split short exact sequence into the 3 x 3 template produced by a section or retraction. The nine lemma recovers the missing exact row, and the published splitting-lemma statement identifies the resulting biproduct data.

items.title: Noether isomorphism theorems recovered from the nine lemma
items.strategy: Place the already-published quotient and canonical-factorization data into a 3 x 3 diagram and let the nine lemma identify the missing exact row. The theorem records the route rather than restating the already-published statements.

items.title: The pullback and pushout theorems
items.strategy: Gather the already-published pullback-of-epi, kernel-transfer, and exact-square criteria into the precise named package used later in the diagram-lemma arguments, and add the dual pushout statement by passage to the opposite category.

items.title: The diagram lemmas hold in the opposite category
items.strategy: Pass each lemma to the opposite category, use that the opposite of an abelian category is abelian, and match the dual statement back to one of the named lemmas already proved on this page.

items.title: An exact functor transports every diagram lemma
items.strategy: Use the exact-functor criterion to obtain the canonical kernel and cokernel comparison isomorphisms, transport the snake data and the pullback or pushout constructions across the functor, and then invoke uniqueness of the connecting morphism to force the transported diagrams to commute.

items.title: Five lemma for a morphism of long exact sequences
items.strategy: Apply the sharp five lemma degreewise to the interior five-term windows of the ladder. The statement is recorded once with the hypotheses packaged globally so later pages can cite it directly.

items.title: FALSE: the connecting morphism depends on the choices made in its construction
items.strategy: Refute the claim by pointing back to the universal-property construction: the connecting map exists and is unique before any member-zig-zag description is mentioned, so there are no choices left for the final morphism to depend on.

items.title: FALSE: the five lemma needs only that the two middle maps are monic
items.strategy: Refute the claim by citing the sharp five lemma and the bookkeeping remark: one half of the argument needs monicity and the other needs epimorphy on the middle comparisons, so monicity alone cannot support the isomorphism conclusion.

items.title: FALSE: the middle nine lemma holds without assuming the composite is zero
items.strategy: Refute the claim by isolating the missing hypothesis from the middle-row variant itself: without the zero composite, the candidate middle row need not even be a complex, so exactness is not a meaningful target.

items.title: FALSE: the snake lemma is just a pair of short exact kernel and cokernel rows
items.strategy: Refute the claim by combining the earlier counterexample to kernel-row short exactness with the positive snake theorem. The missing connecting morphism and the exactness at its source are precisely the extra content.

items.title: FALSE: the diagram lemmas in an abelian category follow from the module case by the embedding theorem
items.strategy: Refute the claim by naming all three defects in the reduction route: the embedding theorem is only proved for small abelian categories, it is not proved on this page, and the connecting-arrow construction is exactly the place where the library insists on an intrinsic abelian proof.

title: The Diagram Lemmas in an Abelian Category — Examples

items.title: The published module five lemma as an instance
items.strategy: Match the categorical hypotheses and conclusion term by term with the already-published module theorem, so the B page exhibits the module statement as the literal instance rather than as a reproof.

items.title: The published module snake lemma as an instance
items.strategy: Place the categorical snake statement next to the already-published module snake lemma and verify that the kernel, cokernel, and connecting-map terms coincide under the module interpretation.

items.title: The published module four lemma as an instance
items.strategy: Read the two halves of the categorical four lemma in the module category and compare them directly with the already-published module statement.

items.title: The connecting morphism computed for a short exact sequence of abelian groups
items.strategy: Choose a concrete two-row short exact diagram in Ab, carry out the pullback-pushout construction explicitly, and identify the resulting connecting map with the familiar quotient homomorphism.

items.title: The snake lemma applied to multiplication by an integer
items.strategy: Apply the snake lemma to the multiplication-by-n ladder in abelian groups and compute the resulting six-term exact sequence explicitly, so the connecting map and endpoint clauses are both visible.

items.title: The nine lemma verified on a diagram of cyclic groups
items.strategy: Write down a 3 x 3 diagram of cyclic groups whose rows and columns can all be checked by hand, then verify the remaining row exactness directly and compare it with the nine lemma.

items.title: A snake configuration whose kernel row is not short exact
items.strategy: Reuse the published multiplication-by-two counterexample from the exactness page. The point here is not to repeat the earlier failure, but to show exactly how the snake lemma repairs it by adding the connecting morphism.

items.title: The short five lemma chased with members
items.strategy: Work through one concrete short exact diagram in abelian groups using the member rules rather than ordinary elements, so the page's thesis that members are a convenience and not a crutch is visible in an actual chase.
